- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Classify beads-tracker issue stubs into themes. Input file (TSV: bead-id, upstream-url, type, priority, title):
/tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/0cfae7ae-f32b-4ece-8102-f6c52d6a5649/scratchpad/triclaim-inventory.tsv

Rules:
- If the upstream-url contains "/pull/", theme is `pr-mirror` regardless of title.
- Otherwise assign exactly ONE theme from this taxonomy, judged from the title (these are all issues about the `bd` CLI issue tracker backed by Dolt):
  - `server-mode` — shared-server / proxied-server / sql-server connection lifecycle, unreachable-server write loss, server identity, auto-start, ports
  - `import-export` — JSONL auto-import/auto-export, issues.jsonl, export fidelity/round-trip, --from-jsonl
  - `sync-remote` — bd dolt push/pull, remotes, clone, bootstrap, backup remotes, federation
  - `migration-schema` — schema migrations, migration gates, dolt version compatibility, schema-init
  - `deps-ready` — bd ready semantics, dependency edges, blocked/is_blocked state, parent-child hierarchy
  - `doctor` — bd doctor checks and --fix behavior
  - `hooks-install` — git hooks, core.hooksPath, install/uninstall artifacts
  - `concurrency` — races, locks, concurrent sessions, simultaneous claims, stale reads
  - `data-integrity` — silent write no-ops, lost updates, corruption, ghost records (when not clearly server-mode-specific)
  - `test-ci` — test flakes, CI-only failures
  - `cli-ux` — flag handling, output formatting, --json shape, error messages, misc UX
  - `misc` — anything else
- When several themes could fit, pick the dominant failure domain (e.g. "writes lost when server unreachable" → server-mode, not data-integrity).

# Review: gastownhall/beads#4504 — drain CALL DOLT_* result sets + 0040/0041 idempotency repair

Head `d285748d5` (single commit, authored 2026-07-05). Merge base with `upstream/main` is `86ccd7ce7`; main has moved 19 commits in `internal/storage/schema/` since. CI on the PR is fully green — but against a base that is three weeks stale.

Worktree: `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4504-review`
Diff: 6 files, +503/−30.

---

## 1. A/B partition

### Part A — drain pattern (mechanically self-contained)

| File | Lines (PR head) | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 967–970 | `procedureCallRe` classifier |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 972–1010 | `drainCall` helper |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 1012–1022 | `execMigrationBody` |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 416 | `MigrateUp` final `DOLT_COMMIT` → `drainCall` |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 478 | `unstagePreExistingTables` `DOLT_RESET(?)` → `drainCall` |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 648 | `stageSchemaTables` `DOLT_ADD('-f', ?)` → `drainCall` |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 1105 | `runMigrations` body apply → `execMigrationBody` |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_body_drain_test.go` | 1–68 | `TestProcedureCallReClassifiesStatements`, `TestMigrationsWithProcedureCallsTakeDrainPath` |
| `internal/storage/schema/lock_test.go` | 168–174 | `ExpectExec` → `ExpectQuery` for DOLT_ADD/DOLT_COMMIT |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema_test.go` | 817–819, 845–850 | `ExpectExec` → `ExpectQuery` for DOLT_ADD/DOLT_RESET |

### Part B — 0040/0041 idempotency repair (contested)

| File | Lines (PR head) | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 20–26 | `repairKey` type |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 28–45 | `preMigrationRepairs` map + rewritten dispatch |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 47–52 | `repairV53RigAndSplitTargets` (pure extraction of the old `case 53`) |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 54–75 | `nonlocalFrozenRows*` consts, `anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 77–113 | `repairPartial0040NonlocalInsert` |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 115–133 | `repairPartial0041NonlocalDelete` |
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_body_drain_test.go` | 70–122 | `TestFrozenNonIdempotentMigrationsHaveRepairs` |
| `internal/storage/dolt/initschema_idempotent_test.go` | 1–183 (whole file) | Both integration tests are B-only |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema_test.go` | 1030–1036, 1063–1075 | Test bound 52 → 39 (needed by **both**: 39 dodges 40/41's CALL bodies *and* their repairs) |

**Coupling:** B depends on A only for the `drainCall` symbol (`migration_repairs.go:100,128`). Substituting `db.ExecContext` there makes B standalone. The `repairKey`/map refactor (B) is independent of the nonlocal repairs and is the piece that carries all the merge pain — it is arguably a third slice, and it is the *only* part of the diff that is pure restructuring with no behavior change.

---

## 2. Part A on its merits

### A-1 (should-fix): the stated root-cause mechanism is not supported by the driver source

`internal/storage/schema/schema.go:978-986` asserts:

> "ExecContext relies on the MySQL driver's internal multi-result discard to consume them. Over a shared Dolt sql-server under concurrent init load that discard has been observed to leave the connection holding an unconsumed proc result set."

That is not what go-sql-driver v1.10.0 does. `mysqlConn.exec` (`connection.go:458-483`) skips columns, skips rows, then calls `handleOk.discardResults()`; `discardResults` (`packets.go:1245-1263`) loops until `statusMoreResultsExists` clears. `mysqlStmt.Exec` (`statement.go:92`) does the same. And the repo's DSN sets `InterpolateParams: true` (`internal/storage/doltutil/dsn.go:57`), so the `?`-bearing calls at `schema.go:478,648` go through COM_QUERY text protocol on *both* Exec and Query — protocol-identical.

The one genuine asymmetry, which the PR does not name, is the **error path**: `mysqlConn.exec` returns early from `readResultSetHeaderPacket`/`skipColumns`/`skipRows` **without** reaching `discardResults()`, whereas `mysqlRows.Close()` (`rows.go:100-127`) always runs `skipRows()` + `discardResults()`. For a multi-statement CALL-bearing body (0040 is 8 statements, 4 of them `CALL DOLT_COMMIT`) that errors mid-stream — e.g. "nothing to commit" on statement 4 with more results queued — Exec can leave packets buffered and Query+Close cannot. That is a plausible busy-buffer mechanism and it is a real argument for `execMigrationBody`. It is *not* an argument for the three single-statement conversions.

Suggested fix: rewrite the doc comment to the error-path argument and drop the unverifiable "has been observed" claim. This matters because the comment is the only justification a future reader will have for a pattern that otherwise looks like cargo cult.

### A-2 (should-fix): the conversion is incomplete on today's main — and the gaps are now the hot sites

Main has 8 `CALL DOLT_*` Exec sites in `internal/storage/schema/`; the PR (written against the older base) converts 3. Left undrained on the **same pinned migration connection**:

- `internal/storage/schema/schema.go:1305` and `:1309` — `commitMigrationStep`'s `DOLT_ADD('-f', ?)` / `DOLT_COMMIT('-m', ?)`. This is per-migration-step now, so on a fresh init it is *N×* more CALL traffic than everything the PR converts combined, and it is the last thing to run before the next migration body.
- `internal/storage/schema/schema.go:302,305` — `commitSeededDoltIgnore`, which runs on the pinned conn immediately before the migration pass (#4744).
- `internal/storage/schema/lock.go:104` — see §6.

If the mechanism is real, these are now the highest-value conversions and part A as written is a half-measure. If it is not real, part A is decoration. Either way the rebase must extend the conversion; landing A verbatim on today's main is the worst of both.

(Repo-wide there are 116 `Exec("CALL …")` sites, mostly in `internal/storage/dolt/`. Those run on pooled connections rather than a pinned session and are legitimately out of scope — worth saying so explicitly in the PR so nobody reads the partial conversion as an oversight.)

### A-3 (nit): `drainCall` is correct

`schema.go:992-1010`. The `for rows.Next() {}` / `NextResultSet()` loop terminating on `rows.Err()` is right: `database/sql` records a later-result-set error in `lasterr`, `NextResultSet()` returns false, and `rows.Err()` surfaces it. So `MigrateUp`'s `strings.Contains(…, "nothing to commit")` tolerance at `schema.go:417` still works. `defer rows.Close()` discarding its error is fine here because the loop already drained.

### A-4 (nit): the classifier could be deleted

`procedureCallRe` (`schema.go:970`) + `execMigrationBody` (`schema.go:1016-1022`) + `TestProcedureCallReClassifiesStatements` is ~60 lines whose only job is to avoid routing 57 of 59 migration bodies through `Query`. Always calling `drainCall` for every migration body would delete all of it and remove the false-negative class entirely. The trade-off is blast radius (every DDL body changes execution path), which is a defensible reason to keep the gate — but it should be a stated choice, not an unexamined one. Note the classifier is verified against the real embedded migrations by `TestMigrationsWithProcedureCallsTakeDrainPath`, and I confirmed on `upstream/main` that 0040 and 0041 are still the only `.up.sql` files containing a statement-initial `CALL`, so the gate is currently exact.

### A-5 (verified): tests pass at PR head

`CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/schema/...` → `ok … 3.402s`.

---

## 3. Part B against the mybd-efzs / #4800 caveat

**The caveat is accurate and the reporter tested this exact head.** gastownhall/beads#4800 (dhruv-pratap) says: reproduced with a build from #4504 (`d285748`). On dolt sql-server 2.1.10, `INSERT`/`DELETE` on `dolt_nonlocal_tables` produce **zero** `dolt_status` diff, so 0040's shipped `CALL DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', …)` — which has no `--skip-empty` and cannot be edited (content-hash frozen) — throws `nothing to commit` on the *first* row, on a *pristine* database. The store never reaches v40.

Against that failure mode:

- **Does B assume staged mutations?** Yes, but only in its own commits, and both use `--skip-empty` (`migration_repairs.go:100-102, 128-130`), so B's commits degrade to a clean no-op rather than an error.
- **Does B break on 2.1.10 server mode?** No. `repairPartial0040NonlocalInsert` guards on `anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` (`migration_repairs.go:69-75`); on the #4800 store the count is 0, so the repair short-circuits before touching anything. Same for the v41 repair (never reached).
- **Does B *fix* 2.1.10 server mode?** No. It is a strict no-op there. The bead's "CONTESTED" label is right in the sense of *insufficient*, not *wrong*.

**But B is not redundant either**, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong when reading only #4800: the partial-0040 replay it targets is a real hole that nothing on main covers. 0040 self-commits each of its four rows (`migrations/0040_ignored_tables_also_nonlocal_tables.up.sql`), and main's `commitEachStep` (`schema.go:1152`) records the cursor row in a *separate* commit afterward. A death in that window leaves committed nonlocal rows with no cursor row. On retry:

- the replay fails with `duplicate primary key given: [wisps]`, which is **not** a `*DirtyTablesError`, so #5042's fresh-bootstrap heal at `lock.go:96` never fires; and
- even if it did fire, `DOLT_RESET('--hard')` discards the *working set* — the offending rows are already **committed**, so the reset cannot remove them.

So B covers a genuine non-converging brick that #5042 explicitly does not. It is narrower than the PR claims (per-step commit shrank the window), but not empty.

### B-1 (should-fix): `DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', …)` in a repair sweeps the whole working set

`migration_repairs.go:100-102` and `:128-130` use `-A`. The doc comment at `:60-67` argues the `present`/`!present` guard makes this safe, and on the production path (`commitEachStep == true`, `schema.go:1152`) prior steps are already committed so the working set is near-empty. But `commitEachStep` is **false** whenever `upTo != 0` — the `mainSource.migrate(ctx, db, maxVersion)` path at `schema.go:394` (remote-migrate gate). On that path migrations 1…39 sit uncommitted in the working set and a firing v40 repair would sweep them into a commit labelled `repair: clear partial 0040 nonlocal rows before replay`. Not corrupting (the cursor rows ride along), but it silently converts a bounded-migrate pass into a committed one under a misleading message. Suggested fix: scope the stage explicitly (`CALL DOLT_ADD('-f','dolt_nonlocal_tables')` then `DOLT_COMMIT('-m', …, '--skip-empty')`), or, if Dolt refuses to `DOLT_ADD` a system table, say so in the comment and gate the repair on `commitEachStep`.

### B-2 (nit): the repair adds a new hard failure point on every fresh init

`anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dolt_nonlocal_tables` before v40 on **every** database with v40 pending. Any engine/backend where that system table is absent now aborts at "pre-repair for migration 0040" instead of at 0040's own INSERT. Roughly equivalent outcome, but the error string moves and gets less specific; worth a wrapped-error note given the new multi-backend work on main (`3f0474a13`).

### B-3 (credit where due)

`TestFrozenNonIdempotentMigrationsHaveRepairs` (`migration_body_drain_test.go:70-122`) is the best thing in the diff. It derives the "needs a repair" set from the embedded migration bytes rather than a hard-coded list, so a future non-idempotent nonlocal migration fails the build. That test is worth keeping even if the two repairs themselves are reworked.

---

## 4. Merge conflict inventory vs `upstream/main` (`08553b8ad`)

`git merge-tree --write-tree --messages upstream/main HEAD` → tree `1af9b5d86`, three conflicted files, six hunks.

| File | Hunk | Severity | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/storage/schema/migration_repairs.go` | 1 (merged lines 41–150) | **Substantive** | Main rewrote the same dispatch: added `case 47: ensureWispTablesForMixedBlockedRecompute` and appended `ensureDependenciesIDColumn` to `case 53`. PR replaced the whole switch with the `preMigrationRepairs` map. Same code, two rewrites. Resolution: keep the map, add `{"schema_migrations", 47}: ensureWispTablesForMixedBlockedRecompute`, and fold `ensureDependenciesIDColumn` into `repairV53RigAndSplitTargets`. Mechanical but must be done by hand and is easy to silently drop a repair. |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` | 1 (merged 1280–1291) | **Trivial** | Main added `preMigrationRepair` dispatch + `Applying migration %04d` progress + timing; PR changed one line `ExecContext` → `execMigrationBody`. Take main's block, swap the one call. |
| `internal/storage/schema/schema_test.go` | 3 (merged 1913/1968/1993) | **Trivial** | Main moved the `mockDB` bound 52→46 and added an `issueRowCounter` stub; PR moved it 52→39. Take main's block with bound 39. |
| `internal/storage/schema/lock_test.go` | — | auto-merges clean | |

The three `drainCall` conversions in `schema.go` (416/478/648) **auto-merge clean** — they are still `db.ExecContext` at `upstream/main:internal/storage/schema/schema.go:567,629,799`. Likewise the `ExpectExec`→`ExpectQuery` test edits auto-merge and remain consistent with the converted production functions (the `ExpectExec` mocks that survive at `schema_test.go:78,80,487,489,491` and `lock_test.go:123,125,205,207,245,248` all target *unconverted* call sites, so the merged test file is internally coherent).

### C-1 (blocker for any naive resolution): a non-conflicting test on main will panic after the merge

`upstream/main:internal/storage/schema/schema_test.go:1996` `TestRunMigrationsLargeRigNoticeOnlyOnMainSource` calls `runMigrations(…, &mockDB{}, mainSource, 0, 46, false)` at lines 2003 and 2014. It is **outside every conflict region**, so git will merge it silently at bound 46. Post-merge that pass reaches migrations 40 and 41, which now route through `execMigrationBody` → `drainCall` → `mockDB.QueryContext`, and through `preMigrationRepairs[40/41]` → `anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` → `mockDB.QueryRowContext`. Both are `panic("not called")` stubs (`schema_test.go:1893-1905`). The test panics.

Fix: lower both bounds to 39, exactly as the PR did for the two tests it knew about. This is the single most likely thing a rebase gets wrong, because the compiler and the conflict markers both stay silent.

---

## 5. Recommended landing strategy

**(ii-variant) Maintainer split-land, but rework rather than cherry-pick — and offer it to the author first.**

Rationale:

- **The conflicts are not the real problem; staleness of the *premise* is.** Part A as written converts three call sites that were the whole story in July 5's `schema.go`. Since then main grew `commitMigrationStep` and `commitSeededDoltIgnore` on the same pinned connection, and #5042 added `DOLT_RESET('--hard')` in `lock.go`. A pure rebase produces a patch that is internally inconsistent with its own thesis (A-2). Asking the contributor to rebase gets us a conflict-free diff that still needs a design conversation.
- **The `repairKey` map refactor is the entire merge cost and buys nothing behavioral.** It exists so `TestFrozenNonIdempotentMigrationsHaveRepairs` can introspect the registry. That is a good reason, but it collides head-on with two independent rewrites of the same switch. Landing the map is the expensive part of the diff and the least of its value.
- **Attribution is cheap and the author earned it.** Rome-1 independently diagnosed the poisoning chain, responded to `kevglynn`'s over-engineering pass within 12 hours, and *revised the whole approach* on 2026-07-05 in response to the content_hash/fork-skew objection rather than defending it. That is exactly the contributor behavior the guidelines say to protect.

Concretely:

1. **Post a `COMMENT` review (not `CHANGES_REQUESTED`)** on #4504 with: the A/B split, the A-1 mechanism correction, the A-2 missed sites, the #4800 relationship stated fairly (B is *insufficient*, not *wrong*, and covers a hole #5042 does not), and the C-1 test-panic trap. Per PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md:64, **offer first**: *"Want to take these, or shall I push them?"* — the author is demonstrably responsive and this is their second substantive revision.
2. **If they take it**, the ask is one PR, rebased, with A extended to `commitMigrationStep`, `commitSeededDoltIgnore` and `lock.go:104`, and both `mockDB` bounds at 39.
3. **If no response in ~72h**, land it in two maintainer commits on a topic branch, both with `Co-authored-by: Rome-1 <…>` and `Closes/Refs #4504`:
   - **Commit 1 (part A+):** `drainCall` + `execMigrationBody` + the classifier, the three original conversions, **plus** `schema.go:1305,1309`, `schema.go:302,305`, `lock.go:104`, plus the two classifier tests and the mock conversions. Rewritten doc comment per A-1. This is small, mechanically verifiable, and has no dependency on the contested half.
   - **Commit 2 (part B):** the `repairKey` registry (re-applied over main's 47/53 repairs), the two nonlocal repairs with the `-Am` scoping fixed per B-1, `TestFrozenNonIdempotentMigrationsHaveRepairs`, and `initschema_idempotent_test.go`. Land this **only after** deciding it on its own merits; it is independently defensible (see §3) but should not ride A's coattails.
4. **File a bead for gastownhall/beads#4800** linking mybd-efzs, noting explicitly that landing #4504 does **not** close it and that the tractable option is the issue's own suggestion (1): a v40 repair that records the cursor row without depending on the shipped COMMIT producing a diff.
5. Do **not** close #4504 in the same action as the disposition comment (PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md:68-75).

Not recommended: **(iii) land whole** — C-1 alone makes the merge red, and B-1 ships a working-set sweep on the remote-migrate path. **(i) rebase + split by the author** as the *only* ask — reasonable, but it front-loads three weeks of drift onto a contributor for a patch whose thesis also needs extending; offer it, don't require it.

---

## 6. Follow-up: #5042's `CALL DOLT_RESET` still lacks the drain

Confirmed. `upstream/main:internal/storage/schema/lock.go:104`:

```go
if _, resetErr := conn.ExecContext(ctx, "CALL DOLT_RESET('--hard')"); resetErr != nil {
    return applied, errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("schema: fresh-bootstrap reset: %w", resetErr))
}
applied, err = MigrateUp(ctx, conn)
```

This is the single strongest candidate in the codebase for the drain pattern, on #4504's own theory:

- it is on the **pinned** migration connection (`conn`, holding `GET_LOCK`);

## 2. Part A on its merits

### A-1 (should-fix): the stated root-cause mechanism is not supported by the driver source

`internal/storage/schema/schema.go:978-986` asserts:

> "ExecContext relies on the MySQL driver's internal multi-result discard to consume them. Over a shared Dolt sql-server under concurrent init load that discard has been observed to leave the connection holding an unconsumed proc result set."

That is not what go-sql-driver v1.10.0 does. `mysqlConn.exec` (`connection.go:458-483`) skips columns, skips rows, then calls `handleOk.discardResults()`; `discardResults` (`packets.go:1245-1263`) loops until `statusMoreResultsExists` clears. `mysqlStmt.Exec` (`statement.go:92`) does the same. And the repo's DSN sets `InterpolateParams: true` (`internal/storage/doltutil/dsn.go:57`), so the `?`-bearing calls at `schema.go:478,648` go through COM_QUERY text protocol on *both* Exec and Query — protocol-identical.

The one genuine asymmetry, which the PR does not name, is the **error path**: `mysqlConn.exec` returns early from `readResultSetHeaderPacket`/`skipColumns`/`skipRows` **without** reaching `discardResults()`, whereas `mysqlRows.Close()` (`rows.go:100-127`) always runs `skipRows()` + `discardResults()`. For a multi-statement CALL-bearing body (0040 is 8 statements, 4 of them `CALL DOLT_COMMIT`) that errors mid-stream — e.g. "nothing to commit" on statement 4 with more results queued — Exec can leave packets buffered and Query+Close cannot. That is a plausible busy-buffer mechanism and it is a real argument for `execMigrationBody`. It is *not* an argument for the three single-statement conversions.

Suggested fix: rewrite the doc comment to the error-path argument and drop the unverifiable "has been observed" claim. This matters because the comment is the only justification a future reader will have for a pattern that otherwise looks like cargo cult.

### A-2 (should-fix): the conversion is incomplete on today's main — and the gaps are now the hot sites

Main has 8 `CALL DOLT_*` Exec sites in `internal/storage/schema/`; the PR (written against the older base) converts 3. Left undrained on the **same pinned migration connection**:

This is per-migration-step now, so on a fresh init it is *N×* more CALL traffic than everything the PR converts combined, and it is the last thing to run before the next migration body.
- `internal/storage/schema/schema.go:302,305` — `commitSeededDoltIgnore`, which runs on the pinned conn immediately before the migration pass (#4744).
- `internal/storage/schema/lock.go:104` — see §6.

If the mechanism is real, these are now the highest-value conversions and part A as written is a half-measure. If it is not real, part A is decoration. Either way the rebase must extend the conversion; landing A verbatim on today's main is the worst of both.

(Repo-wide there are 116 `Exec("CALL …")` sites, mostly in `internal/storage/dolt/`. Those run on pooled connections rather than a pinned session and are legitimately out of scope — worth saying so explicitly in the PR so nobody reads the partial conversion as an oversight.)

`schema.go:992-1010`. The `for rows.Next() {}` / `NextResultSet()` loop terminating on `rows.Err()` is right: `database/sql` records a later-result-set error in `lasterr`, `NextResultSet()` returns false, and `rows.Err()` surfaces it. ## 3. Part B against the mybd-efzs / #4800 caveat

**The caveat is accurate and the reporter tested this exact head.** gastownhall/beads#4800 (dhruv-pratap) says: reproduced with a build from #4504 (`d285748`). On dolt sql-server 2.1.10, `INSERT`/`DELETE` on `dolt_nonlocal_tables` produce **zero** `dolt_status` diff, so 0040's shipped `CALL DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', …)` — which has no `--skip-empty` and cannot be edited (content-hash frozen) — throws `nothing to commit` on the *first* row, on a *pristine* database. The store never reaches v40.

Against that failure mode:

- **Does B assume staged mutations?** Yes, but only in its own commits, and both use `--skip-empty` (`migration_repairs.go:100-102, 128-130`), so B's commits degrade to a clean no-op rather than an error.
- **Does B break on 2.1.10 server mode?** No. `repairPartial0040NonlocalInsert` guards on `anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` (`migration_repairs.go:69-75`); on the #4800 store the count is 0, so the repair short-circuits before touching anything. Same for the v41 repair (never reached).
- **Does B *fix* 2.1.10 server mode?** No. It is a strict no-op there. The bead's "CONTESTED" label is right in the sense of *insufficient*, not *wrong*.

**But B is not redundant either**, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong when reading only #4800: the partial-0040 replay it targets is a real hole that nothing on main covers. 0040 self-commits each of its four rows (`migrations/0040_ignored_tables_also_nonlocal_tables.up.sql`), and main's `commitEachStep` (`schema.go:1152`) records the cursor row in a *separate* commit afterward. A death in that window leaves committed nonlocal rows with no cursor row. On retry:

- the replay fails with `duplicate primary key given: [wisps]`, which is **not** a `*DirtyTablesError`, so #5042's fresh-bootstrap heal at `lock.go:96` never fires; and
- even if it did fire, `DOLT_RESET('--hard')` discards the *working set* — the offending rows are already **committed**, so the reset cannot remove them.

So B covers a genuine non-converging brick that #5042 explicitly does not. It is narrower than the PR claims (per-step commit shrank the window), but not empty.

### B-1 (should-fix): `DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', …)` in a repair sweeps the whole working set

`migration_repairs.go:100-102` and `:128-130` use `-A`. The doc comment at `:60-67` argues the `present`/`!present` guard makes this safe, and on the production path (`commitEachStep == true`, `schema.go:1152`) prior steps are already committed so the working set is near-empty. But `commitEachStep` is **false** whenever `upTo != 0` — the `mainSource.migrate(ctx, db, maxVersion)` path at `schema.go:394` (remote-migrate gate). On that path migrations 1…39 sit uncommitted in the working set and a firing v40 repair would sweep them into a commit labelled `repair: clear partial 0040 nonlocal rows before replay`. Not corrupting (the cursor rows ride along), but it silently converts a bounded-migrate pass into a committed one under a misleading message. Suggested fix: scope the stage explicitly (`CALL DOLT_ADD('-f','dolt_nonlocal_tables')` then `DOLT_COMMIT('-m', …, '--skip-empty')`), or, if Dolt refuses to `DOLT_ADD` a system table, say so in the comment and gate the repair on `commitEachStep`.

`anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dolt_nonlocal_tables` before v40 on **every** database with v40 pending. Any engine/backend where that system table is absent now aborts at "pre-repair for migration 0040" instead of at 0040's own INSERT. Roughly equivalent outcome, but the error string moves and gets less specific; worth a wrapped-error note given the new multi-backend work on main (`3f0474a13`).

`TestFrozenNonIdempotentMigrationsHaveRepairs` (`migration_body_drain_test.go:70-122`) is the best thing in the diff. That is not what go-sql-driver v1.10.0 does. `mysqlConn.exec` (`connection.go:458-483`) skips columns, skips rows, then calls `handleOk.discardResults()`; `discardResults` (`packets.go:1245-1263`) loops until `statusMoreResultsExists` clears. `mysqlStmt.Exec` (`statement.go:92`) does the same. The one genuine asymmetry, which the PR does not name, is the **error path**: `mysqlConn.exec` returns early from `readResultSetHeaderPacket`/`skipColumns`/`skipRows` **without** reaching `discardResults()`, whereas `mysqlRows.Close()` (`rows.go:100-127`) always runs `skipRows()` + `discardResults()`. `schema.go:992-1010`. That's a solid argument for `execMigrationBody` on multi-statement CALL-bearing bodies; it's not an argument for the three single-statement conversions. Suggest rewriting the comment to the error-path argument.
2. **The conversion is now incomplete — and the gaps are the hot sites.** Since your base, main added more `CALL DOLT_*` Exec sites on the same pinned migration connection: `commitMigrationStep` (per-step `DOLT_ADD`/`DOLT_COMMIT` — N× more CALL traffic than everything the PR converts), `commitSeededDoltIgnore`, and #5042's `DOLT_RESET('--hard')` in `lock.go` (which is immediately followed by a full `MigrateUp` on that same conn — the strongest candidate in the codebase on your own theory). A rebased part A should extend to those.
3. **Rebase trap (would-be red merge):** main's `TestRunMigrationsLargeRigNoticeOnlyOnMainSource` calls `runMigrations` with bound 46 and sits *outside* every conflict region, so git merges it silently — post-merge it reaches 40/41, routes through `drainCall`/`anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent`, and panics on the `mockDB` stubs. Both bounds need lowering to 39, exactly as you did for the two tests you knew about.

- Re #4800 (dhruv-pratap reproduced `nothing to commit` on dolt 2.1.10 server mode with a build of this PR): the repairs are a strict **no-op** there — `anyNonlocalFrozenRowPresent` short-circuits on a pristine store — so B is *insufficient* for that failure, but not *wrong*.
```go
temp := fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d", r.Parent, 1_000_000+i)
if err := renameSubtreeInTx(ctx, tx, r.OldID, temp); err != nil { // remote -> temp
```

If `parent.1000000` itself exists you get a duplicate-key error (fails safe, confusing message). If a *descendant* exists — `parent.1000000.5` — step 1 succeeds (no dup on the root), and step 3's `renameSubtreeInTx(temp, r.NewID)` sweeps the bystander into the swapped subtree. Confirmed:

```
bystander: tp-p.1000000.5 title="" ; tp-p.74.5 title="Bystander"
```

An unrelated issue was silently relocated and the rebase reported success. Exotic, but it is silent data movement in the command's own reconcile path. Fix: before the swap, assert no id matching `temp` or `temp.%` exists in `issues` or `wisps` (one `SELECT COUNT(*)`), and bump `temp` until free, or derive it from `maxChildNumber+1` in the same free-number allocator the renumber already owns rather than a magic constant.

## SHOULD-FIX 6 — `resolveChildCountersToHighWater` no-ops silently when our side deleted the counter row

`internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:531-578`. The parent is read via `COALESCE(our_parent_id, their_parent_id, base_parent_id)` (`:533`), so a delete/modify conflict yields the parent from *their* side; the subsequent `UPDATE child_counters SET last_child = ? WHERE parent_id = ?` (`:566-567`) then affects zero rows, and `DOLT_CONFLICTS_RESOLVE('--ours', ...)` (`:572`) keeps the deletion. The counter is gone, `GetNextChildIDTx` restarts from the `issues` scan, and the very duplicate-minting this command fixes can recur. Use the same upsert as `:294-297` and check `RowsAffected`.

Also at `:537`: `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "dolt_conflicts_child_counters")` swallows *any* error mentioning the table, including a genuine query failure. `dberrors` is already imported (`:11`) — use `dberrors.IsTableNotExist(err)`.

## SHOULD-FIX 7 — file-header comment describes behavior the code does not have

`internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:47-51`: *"content_hash is set NULL on every renumbered row."* Nothing in this PR touches `content_hash`; `issueops.updateIssueIDInTx` (`internal/storage/issueops/bulk_ops.go:233-244`) updates only id/title/description/design/acceptance_criteria/notes/updated_at. And it would be unnecessary anyway — `Issue.ComputeContentHash` (`internal/types/types.go:158-161`) *excludes* the ID by design. On a data-corruption-adjacent path a comment asserting a safety measure that does not exist is worse than no comment. Delete the paragraph.

## SHOULD-FIX 8 — the open coverage gaps from the previous round are all still open

- **No test touches `RebaseRemote` on either store.** `grep -rn RebaseRemote` outside the interface finds only `cmd/bd/dolt.go:630`, `internal/storage/dolt/store.go:3134`, `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/version_control.go:445`. The `readOnly` guard, the `remote + "/" + s.branch` tracking-ref construction, the `commitBeforePull`/`CommitPending` ordering relative to the backup tag, and `recomputeBlockedAfterPull` are entirely unexercised. The three embedded tests call `versioncontrolops.RebaseChildCollisions` directly against a peer *branch*.
- **No two-clone pull/push convergence test.** The concurrent-rebase story (both clones independently pick the same free `.74`, second push rejected, second rebase must renumber again) is plausible-by-reading but unverified.
- **No CLI/`--json` test, and no `--json` support at all.** `storage.RebaseReport` carries json tags (`internal/storage/versioned.go:44-63`) but `cmd/bd/dolt.go:589-660` never consults the global `jsonOutput` (`cmd/bd/main.go:607`) — `bd dolt rebase --json` prints prose. Cheap and worth doing before merge given agents are the primary consumer.
- **Registration tests not extended.** `cmd/bd/dolt_test.go:790` and `:835` enumerate `{"push","pull","commit"}`; adding `"rebase"` covers the `needsStoreDoltSubcommands` wiring change at `cmd/bd/main.go:889` for free.
- **No discoverability routing.** When a plain pull dies on this exact collision (`internal/storage/dolt/store.go:3392`, `internal/storage/versioncontrolops/mergesettle.go:88/:145`), nothing mentions `bd dolt rebase`, and `bd doctor` has no corresponding check. The command is unreachable unless you already know it exists. A one-line hint on the pull failure path is the minimum.

## NIT 9 — non-deterministic report output

`cmd/bd/dolt.go:653-655` iterates `report.CountersSet` (a map) for user-visible output. `detectCollisions` sorts *"so multi-collision renumbering is reproducible"* (`rebase.go:219-220`); the report should match. Sort the parent keys.

## NIT 10 — no `--dry-run`

For an operator recovery command that mutates history under a backup tag, `--dry-run` printing the planned `old → new` list (everything through `detectCollisions` + `renumberCollisions`'s seeding is already side-effect-free) would be cheap and would materially lower the cost of the remaining risk.

## NIT 11 — backup tags accumulate

`rebase.go:107-112` creates `bd-pre-rebase-<head8>` and never removes it on success (deliberate, per `cmd/bd/dolt.go:648`). Fine, but there is no `bd dolt rebase --clean-backups` or mention in the help text of how to remove them; over time these accumulate in `dolt_tags`. Worth a sentence in the `Long` help.

---

## On CI cost (item 5)

The new tests do **not** land in the conformance job. `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/rebase_collision_test.go` defines plain `TestEmbeddedRebase*` functions, and both `test-embedded-conformance` shards filter with `-test.run '^TestConformance$'` (`.github/workflows/main.yml:883,887`; `.github/workflows/pr-risk.yml:214,218`). They run in `test-embedded-storage`, which uses `-test.skip '^TestConformance$'` (`main.yml:844`) and *is* the at-ceiling job (no `timeout-minutes:`, 30m Go timeout, with the comment at `main.yml:838-841` noting bd-lrgn1 pushed a slow runner past 20m).

Measured cost is negligible: 1.36s + 1.32s + 1.34s = ~4.0s wall for all three, each dominated by one `newTestEnv` store-open/migration chain. Under `-race` in CI, call it 10-15s. Not a concern. If a fourth and fifth test are added for the blockers above, consider folding them into subtests sharing one `testEnv` — note `labelIssue` (`rebase_collision_test.go:174-182`) queries `WHERE label = 'vip'` unscoped, so sharing an env requires per-test label names.

---

## Verdict: request-changes

The design is sound and the mechanic is the right pragmatic shape — renumber the losing side through the canonical rename primitive, settle the counter to the true high-water, keep the derived-PK dependency rekey inside `issueops.UpdateIssueIDInTx` (invariant 3a is genuinely satisfied and directly asserted by `assertDepRekeyed`). The three fixes from the previous round are real work, not cosmetic. But two of them are incomplete in ways I confirmed empirically rather than by reading: the wisp awareness was added to subtree enumeration and not to free-id selection, so the command silently produces the GH#4455 dual-presence corruption it should be preventing (BLOCKER 1); and the atomic-restore guarantee does not cover the untracked wisp tables the fix newly mutates, so the failure path strands orphaned wisps and splits `dependencies`/`wisp_dependencies` while the CLI prints "No changes were kept" (BLOCKER 2). Both are in the exact risk class this PR names — silent data corruption in a sync failure path, on a command an operator only reaches when they are already in trouble — and both are narrowly fixable (a wisps-aware `maxChildNumber` plus counter seeding; and either deferring the wisp rename past the merge or refusing to start with wisps in a colliding subtree). Per PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES this is close enough to landing that absorb-and-fix-locally is the better route than a request-changes round trip if the author is not immediately available — the contributor value is high and the deltas are small — but it must not merge at this head.</result>

# tri:claim backlog drain strategy — theme-clustered sweeps (mybd-xmx7)

2026-07-26. Owner asked for a drain pattern for the tri:claim issue-stub backlog,
analogous to the author-clustered PR sweeps (`author-clustered-pr-sweeps` memory)
but clustered by subsystem/theme instead of author.

## Population

223 open `tri:claim` stubs at design time (pool grew from 52 to 223 with the
2026-07-26 full-pool triage run, `reports/triage/2026-07-26.md`). Every stub now
carries exactly one `theme:<slug>` label (classification pass this session,
haiku-tier, ~57k tokens):

| theme | count | notes |
|-------|------:|-------|
| pr-mirror | 43 | stubs whose upstream ref is a PR — belong to the PR-sweep lane, NOT issue sweeps |
| cli-ux | 36 | flag handling, output/json shape, error messages |
| server-mode | 34 | shared/proxied sql-server lifecycle, unreachable-server write loss |
| misc | 22 | needs a reclassify pass; likely splits into existing themes |
| sync-remote | 17 | bd dolt push/pull, remotes, bootstrap, backup remotes |
| import-export | 13 | JSONL auto-import/export, fidelity, round-trip |
| test-ci | 12 | flakes, CI-only failures |
| migration-schema | 12 | migrations, gates, dolt version compat |
| data-integrity | 11 | silent no-ops, lost updates, ghost records |
| doctor | 7 | bd doctor checks/--fix |
| concurrency | 7 | races, locks, simultaneous claims, stale reads |
| deps-ready | 6 | bd ready semantics, dependency edges |
| hooks-install | 3 | git hooks, core.hooksPath artifacts |

## Sweep unit

One theme, all its stubs, one session, one consolidated report + follow-up
bead. Steps per sweep:

1. **Freshness (delegated, cheap tier):** for every stub, check upstream —
   issue still open? merged PR references it? last comments indicate
   resolution? version-pinned to behavior since rewritten (many stubs are
   v1.0.4-era; current is v1.1.2)? Scout/haiku gathers facts verbatim;
   orchestrator synthesizes.
2. **Dedupe within theme:** stubs frequently share one root cause (e.g. the
   auto-import-on-every-command family). Identify root-cause groups.
3. **Disposition per stub (orchestrator judgment):**
   - `tri-close` — fixed upstream since filing, stale, or dupe (reason names
     the fixing PR / surviving stub). Uses `scripts/tri-close` so the
     `triaged` label lands upstream; text publication stays human-gated via
     `scripts/tri-submit`.
   - **consolidate** — N same-root-cause stubs → ONE actionable engineering
     bead with repro + design; stubs closed as dupes pointing at it.
   - **flesh out** — stub survives alone: add acceptance criteria, repro,
     affected code paths so it stops being a stub.
4. **Report:** `reports/<date>-issue-sweep-<theme>.md` — disposition table +
   root-cause map. One follow-up bead for engineering work that emerged.

## Ordering (proposed)

1. **import-export (13)** — first sweep, this session (proof of pattern).
2. **data-integrity (11) + concurrency (7)** — highest severity density,
   freshness likely kills several (many predate the v1.1.x write-path work).
3. **migration-schema (12)** — warm context from #4504/#5042/mybd-efzs work.
4. **sync-remote (17), doctor (7), deps-ready (6), hooks-install (3)**.
5. **cli-ux (36)** — bulk lane, low risk; batch freshness via one delegated
   pass, dispositions mostly mechanical.
6. **misc (22)** — reclassify first, then fold into the above.
7. **server-mode (34)** — LAST or coordinated: overlaps the active
   local-first/proxied campaign (epic mybd-psxg, in-progress lanes). Sweep
   only dispositions/consolidates; engineering routes into the campaign.
   Check with campaign lane owners before closing anything they may be using
   as evidence.
8. **pr-mirror (43)** — not an issue sweep at all: route to the
   author-clustered PR sweep lane (mybd-8nq5s pattern). The theme label makes
   them separable (`bd list -l theme:pr-mirror`).

## Rules

- Theme labels are durable: future triage runs should theme-label new
  tri:claim stubs at creation (add to `/triage` procedure — follow-up bead).
- A sweep never posts prose upstream except through the human-gated
  `tri-submit`; `tri-close` label-only closes are allowed (existing policy).
- bd writes stay serial; freshness recon parallelizes freely (gh reads).
- Collision guard: before dispositioning a stub, check it isn't referenced by
  an in-progress bead in another session's lane (`bd list --status=in_progress`).

## Verification of the three claimed blocker fixes

### (a) Wisp-aware subtree enumeration — HALF-FIXED

`internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:316-348` really does walk both stores, and `renameSubtreeInTx` (`:354-383`) routes each id via `issueops.IsActiveWispInTx`. The orphan case has a real test (`internal/storage/embeddeddolt/rebase_collision_test.go:278-320`) and it genuinely fails if enumeration is issues-only. That half is correct.

But wisp-awareness was added to **enumeration** and not to **free-id selection**. See BLOCKER 1.

### (b) `hadViol && !repairedViol` abort parity — CORRECT for the violation gate, but the merge-error gate diverges

`rebase.go:496-507` matches `mergesettle.go:132-146` on the violation branch. Parity confirmed. One divergence remains — see SHOULD-FIX 4.

### (c) Atomic hard-reset-to-backup-tag on ANY failure — NOT ATOMIC

Control-flow-wise the defer at `rebase.go:121-129` is installed before the first mutation and every post-tag error path returns through the named `retErr`, so it always fires. But `DOLT_RESET('--hard', <tag>)` only reverts *tracked* tables. See BLOCKER 2 — empirically confirmed.

## BLOCKER 1 — renumber picks an id a session-local wisp already owns (GH#4455 dual-presence corruption, reported as success)

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4844-review/internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:422-442`

```go
query := `
    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(id, '.', -1) AS UNSIGNED)), 0)
    FROM issues%s
    WHERE id LIKE CONCAT(?, '.%%') AND id NOT LIKE CONCAT(?, '.%%.%%')`
```

`maxChildNumber` scans `issues` only. `renumberCollisions` (`:241-263`) seeds the free-number high-water solely from this scan across HEAD + `remoteRef` + `base`; it never consults `wisps` and never consults `child_counters` on either side.

Issues and wisps share one ID space (`internal/storage/embeddeddolt/cross_table_id_collision_test.go:11-17`: *"a dual presence row makes merge-based lookups (bd ready/search) hard-error for the whole store"*), and `issueops.GetNextChildIDTx` (`internal/storage/issueops/child_id.go:9-13`) numbers a wisp child of a **durable** parent off the durable `child_counters`/`issues` space. So a session-local wisp legitimately occupies `parent.N` without appearing in `issues`.

Empirically confirmed against real embedded Dolt (probe: durable parent with a wisp direct child at `.74`, `child_counters.last_child=74`, remote-dominates rebase):

```
id xt-p.74 => issues.title="Local71" wisps.title="WispSibling"
DUAL PRESENCE: xt-p.74 exists in BOTH issues ("Local71") and wisps ("WispSibling")
```

The rebase returned **nil error** — the CLI would print "Rebase complete. Run 'bd dolt push' to share." over a store that now hard-errors on `bd ready`/`bd search`.

The same blind spot recurs at `rebase.go:562` (`resolveChildCountersToHighWater` calls `maxChildNumber(ctx, db, "", p)`), which additionally uses a bare `SET last_child = ?` (`:566-568`) where the sibling path at `:294-297` correctly uses `GREATEST(...)`. So the counter can be *lowered* below an existing wisp child's number, re-arming duplicate minting on the next `bd create --parent`.

Suggested fix: make `maxChildNumber` take the max over `issues` **and** `wisps` (working set only — `AS OF` on a dolt-ignored table is meaningless), and additionally seed `next[parent]` from `GREATEST(scan, child_counters.last_child)` on HEAD and at `remoteRef`/`base`; change `:566` to `SET last_child = GREATEST(last_child, ?)`. Add the probe above as a regression test.

## BLOCKER 2 — the "atomic" restore strands renamed wisps; the CLI then tells the operator nothing was kept

`internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:121-129`

```go
defer func() {
    if retErr == nil { return }
    if _, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, "CALL DOLT_RESET('--hard', ?)", backupTag); err != nil {
```

with the contract stated at `:114-120` (*"leaves the DB exactly as it was found"*).

Wisp tables are `dolt_ignore`'d and never committed (`internal/storage/dolt/schema_parity_test.go:196-218`), i.e. untracked. `DOLT_RESET --hard` follows git semantics and leaves untracked tables alone. Primitive probe:

```
AFTER RESET: issues probe-1=1 probe-9=0 probe-2=0 | wisps probe-1.1=0 probe-9.1=1 total=1
```

End-to-end probe driving the real `RebaseChildCollisions` failure path (unresolvable non-memory `config` conflict, which is exactly the class `TryAutoResolveMergeConflicts` refuses):

```
rebase failed as designed: rebase merge left conflicts in config that require operator resolution; merge aborted
AFTER FAILED REBASE: issues ap-x.71=1 ap-x.74=0 | wisps ap-x.71.1=0 ap-x.74.1=1
dolt_status after failed rebase: []
```

The durable child is correctly back at `.71`, but its wisp child is now permanently at `.74.1` — orphaned under an id that no longer exists. This is precisely the orphan hazard fix (a) was added to prevent, reintroduced on the failure path, and it is caused *by* fix (a): before wisp renaming was added, there was nothing for the reset to miss. Working set reads clean, so nothing surfaces it.

There is a second, worse half: `updateWispIDInTx` also writes `wisp_events` and calls `UpdateWispIDInDependenciesInTx`, which rewrites rows in **both** `wisp_dependencies` (untracked, survives the reset) and `dependencies` (tracked, reverted). The abort therefore leaves the two dependency tables mutually inconsistent, not merely stale.

And `cmd/bd/dolt.go:635-641` reports this as a clean rollback:

```go
fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nThe database was restored to its pre-rebase state (backup tag: %s).\n", report.BackupTag)
fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "No changes were kept; resolve the cause above and retry.")
```

Suggested fix (pick one, in preference order):
1. Snapshot the affected wisp/`wisp_*` rows before the renumber tx and restore them explicitly in the defer alongside the reset — the only option that keeps the stated contract.
2. Perform the durable renumber and the wisp renumber as one *deferred* unit: run the wisp renames only after the merge (and swap) have succeeded, so the failure path has no wisp mutation to undo. `renameSubtreeInTx` already separates the two tables, so this is a reordering, not a rewrite.
3. Minimum acceptable: refuse to start when any wisp row lies inside a colliding subtree (`bd dolt rebase` is an operator recovery command; "commit or discard your wisps first" is a legitimate precondition), and correct the `:114-120` comment and the CLI message.

## SHOULD-FIX 3 — the CLI's restore message is wrong in both directions

- `internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:141` and `:145` return `nil, err` after `report.BackupTag` was already set at `:112`. So for a renumber or renumber-commit failure the CLI's `report != nil && report.BackupTag != ""` branch never fires and the operator is never told the backup tag exists — exactly when they most need it. Return `report, err` at both sites.
- Conversely, `internal/storage/dolt/store.go:3160-3162` and `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/version_control.go:465-467` return `report, err` when only `recomputeBlockedAfterPull` failed. The rebase **succeeded and is committed**, but `cmd/bd/dolt.go:635-641` prints "The database was restored to its pre-rebase state ... No changes were kept". That is a false statement that invites destructive operator action. Add an explicit `Restored bool` to `storage.RebaseReport` set only by the defer in `RebaseChildCollisions`, and gate the CLI message on it.

## SHOULD-FIX 4 — merge-error handling diverges from the pull-settle contract it claims parity with

`internal/storage/versioncontrolops/rebase.go:461-468`

```go
_, mergeErr := db.ExecContext(ctx, "CALL DOLT_MERGE(?)", winRef)
if mergeErr != nil && strings.Contains(mergeErr.Error(), "up to date") { mergeErr = nil }
if mergeErr != nil {
    abortMerge(ctx, db, preMergeClean)
    return fmt.Errorf("merge %s after renumber: %w", winRef, mergeErr)
```

Deep re-review at head d484d2e (two independent review passes, cross-vendor, with empirical probes against real embedded Dolt run in a scratch copy). The design is sound and the three fixes from the previous round are real work — wisp-aware enumeration, abort parity, and the backup-tag defer are all genuinely there. But two of the fixes are incomplete in ways we confirmed by running the code, not just reading it, and both are in this PR's own named risk class: silent data corruption on a sync failure path. Details below.

## Blocker 1 — free-ID selection is wisp-blind: rebase mints an ID a session-local wisp already owns

`maxChildNumber` (rebase.go:422-442) scans `issues` only; `renumberCollisions` seeds the free-number high-water solely from that scan and never consults `wisps` or `child_counters`. A session-local wisp legitimately occupies `parent.N` without appearing in `issues` (`GetNextChildIDTx` numbers wisp children of durable parents off the shared space). Probe (durable parent, wisp child at `.74`, remote-dominates rebase):

```
DUAL PRESENCE: xt-p.74 exists in BOTH issues ("Local71") and wisps ("WispSibling")
```

...and the rebase returned nil — "Rebase complete" over a store that now hard-errors on `bd ready`/`bd search` (the GH#4455 dual-presence class this command exists to clean up). Same blind spot at rebase.go:562, where `resolveChildCountersToHighWater` also uses a bare `SET last_child = ?` (the sibling path at :294-297 correctly uses `GREATEST`), so the counter can be *lowered* below an existing wisp child, re-arming duplicate minting.

Fix shape: `maxChildNumber` takes max over `issues` AND `wisps` (working set), seed from `GREATEST(scan, child_counters.last_child)` on all three refs, `GREATEST` in the :566 update.

## Blocker 2 — the atomic restore strands renamed wisps; CLI then reports a clean rollback

`DOLT_RESET('--hard', <tag>)` in the defer (rebase.go:121-129) only reverts *tracked* tables; `wisps`/`wisp_*` are `dolt_ignore`'d. End-to-end probe driving the real failure path (unresolvable `config` conflict):

```
AFTER FAILED REBASE: issues ap-x.71=1 ap-x.74=0 | wisps ap-x.71.1=0 ap-x.74.1=1
```

The durable child is back at `.71`; its wisp child is stranded at `.74.1` — orphaned under an ID that no longer exists, which is the exact hazard the wisp-enumeration fix was added to prevent, reintroduced on the failure path *by* that fix. Worse: `updateWispIDInTx` rewrites both `wisp_dependencies` (untracked, survives) and `dependencies` (tracked, reverted), so the two dependency tables end mutually inconsistent. And cmd/bd/dolt.go:635-641 prints "No changes were kept" over it.

Fix shape (preference order): (1) snapshot affected wisp rows pre-tx and restore them in the defer; (2) defer the wisp renames until after merge+swap succeed, so the failure path has no wisp mutation to undo (`renameSubtreeInTx` already separates the tables — a reordering, not a rewrite); (3) minimum: refuse to start with wisps inside a colliding subtree and fix the :114-120 contract comment + CLI message.

## Blocker 3 — LIKE wildcards in subtree root IDs are unescaped

rebase.go:333-334 binds the root into a `LIKE CONCAT(?, '.%')` pattern. Explicitly-assigned IDs may contain `_`/`%` (current ID validation permits them), so a collision under `bd-a_b.71` can sweep and rename descendants of `bd-axb.71` — silent relocation of unrelated data. Escape wildcards with an `ESCAPE` clause or use a prefix-safe comparison.

## Should-fixes

- **Restore message wrong in both directions:** rebase.go:141,:145 return `nil, err` after `BackupTag` is set, so on renumber failure the operator is never told the tag exists; conversely store.go:3160/version_control.go:465 return `report, err` when only `recomputeBlockedAfterPull` failed — rebase committed, CLI still prints "restored to pre-rebase state". Add `Restored bool` to `RebaseReport`, set only by the defer; gate the message on it; return `report, err` at :141/:145.
- **Deferred reset runs on the caller's context** (rebase.go:125): a canceled API context means the rollback itself can't execute. Use a bounded detached context for cleanup.
- **Merge-error handling diverges from pull-settle** (rebase.go:461-468): bails immediately where `SettleMerge` deliberately carries `mergeErr` through the settle pass because some Dolt versions error on conflicts. On such builds `bd dolt rebase` could never complete (the `child_counters` conflict is always present). Route through the same shape.
- **Temp ID `parent.1000000+i` has no occupancy check** (rebase.go:401-413): a bystander at `parent.1000000.5` gets silently swept into the swapped subtree (probe-confirmed). Assert `temp`/`temp.%` free in issues+wisps, or allocate from the same free-number pool.
- **Counter delete/modify conflict no-ops silently** (rebase.go:531-578): our-side deletion → `UPDATE` affects 0 rows, `--ours` keeps the deletion, counter gone. Upsert like :294-297 + check `RowsAffected`. Also :537's `strings.Contains(err.Error(), ...)` swallows real errors — use `dberrors.IsTableNotExist`.
- **Header comment claims `content_hash` is nulled on renumber** (rebase.go:47-51) — nothing does that (and it's unnecessary: `ComputeContentHash` excludes ID). On a corruption-adjacent path, an asserted-but-absent safety measure is worse than none. Delete the paragraph.
- **Coverage gaps from the previous round remain:** no test exercises `RebaseRemote` on either store; no two-clone convergence test; `--json` prints prose (report has json tags, CLI never checks `jsonOutput`); registration tests not extended; and nothing routes an operator here — the pull-failure path never mentions `bd dolt rebase`. A one-line hint there is the minimum for discoverability.
- Nits: `CountersSet` map iteration makes report output non-deterministic (sort keys); `--dry-run` would be cheap and worth it for an operator recovery command; backup tags accumulate with no documented cleanup.

CI-cost note: the new tests land in `test-embedded-storage` (~4s wall, negligible), not the at-ceiling conformance shards — no concern there.

## Verdict

Not mergeable at this head — blockers 1 and 2 are confirmed corruption on the command's own recovery path. But the deltas are small relative to the value and the invariants that matter (derived-PK dep rekey via `issueops.UpdateIssueIDInTx`, sorted collision processing, backup-tag mechanics) are genuinely satisfied. Want to take these? If you'd rather we absorb them, we're happy to land maintainer-side fixes on top of your branch with your commits intact — say the word.

Deep re-review at head d484d2e (two independent review passes, cross-vendor, with empirical probes against real embedded Dolt run in a scratch copy). The design is sound and the three fixes from the previous round are real work — wisp-aware enumeration, abort parity, and the backup-tag defer are all genuinely there. But two of the fixes are incomplete in ways we confirmed by running the code, not just reading it, and both are in this PR's own named risk class: silent data corruption on a sync failure path. Details below.

## Blocker 1 — free-ID selection is wisp-blind: rebase mints an ID a session-local wisp already owns

`maxChildNumber` (rebase.go:422-442) scans `issues` only; `renumberCollisions` seeds the free-number high-water solely from that scan and never consults `wisps` or `child_counters`. A session-local wisp legitimately occupies `parent.N` without appearing in `issues` (`GetNextChildIDTx` numbers wisp children of durable parents off the shared space). Probe (durable parent, wisp child at `.74`, remote-dominates rebase):

```
DUAL PRESENCE: xt-p.74 exists in BOTH issues ("Local71") and wisps ("WispSibling")
```

...and the rebase returned nil — "Rebase complete" over a store that now hard-errors on `bd ready`/`bd search` (the GH#4455 dual-presence class this command exists to clean up). Same blind spot at rebase.go:562, where `resolveChildCountersToHighWater` also uses a bare `SET last_child = ?` (the sibling path at :294-297 correctly uses `GREATEST`), so the counter can be *lowered* below an existing wisp child, re-arming duplicate minting.

Fix shape: `maxChildNumber` takes max over `issues` AND `wisps` (working set), seed from `GREATEST(scan, child_counters.last_child)` on all three refs, `GREATEST` in the :566 update.

## Blocker 2 — the atomic restore strands renamed wisps; CLI then reports a clean rollback

`DOLT_RESET('--hard', <tag>)` in the defer (rebase.go:121-129) only reverts *tracked* tables; `wisps`/`wisp_*` are `dolt_ignore`'d. End-to-end probe driving the real failure path (unresolvable `config` conflict):

```
AFTER FAILED REBASE: issues ap-x.71=1 ap-x.74=0 | wisps ap-x.71.1=0 ap-x.74.1=1
```

The durable child is back at `.71`; its wisp child is stranded at `.74.1` — orphaned under an ID that no longer exists, which is the exact hazard the wisp-enumeration fix was added to prevent, reintroduced on the failure path *by* that fix. Worse: `updateWispIDInTx` rewrites both `wisp_dependencies` (untracked, survives) and `dependencies` (tracked, reverted), so the two dependency tables end mutually inconsistent. And cmd/bd/dolt.go:635-641 prints "No changes were kept" over it.

Fix shape (preference order): (1) snapshot affected wisp rows pre-tx and restore them in the defer; (2) defer the wisp renames until after merge+swap succeed, so the failure path has no wisp mutation to undo (`renameSubtreeInTx` already separates the tables — a reordering, not a rewrite); (3) minimum: refuse to start with wisps inside a colliding subtree and fix the :114-120 contract comment + CLI message.

## Blocker 3 — LIKE wildcards in subtree root IDs are unescaped

rebase.go:333-334 binds the root into a `LIKE CONCAT(?, '.%')` pattern. Explicitly-assigned IDs may contain `_`/`%` (current ID validation permits them), so a collision under `bd-a_b.71` can sweep and rename descendants of `bd-axb.71` — silent relocation of unrelated data. Escape wildcards with an `ESCAPE` clause or use a prefix-safe comparison.

## Should-fixes

- **Restore message wrong in both directions:** rebase.go:141,:145 return `nil, err` after `BackupTag` is set, so on renumber failure the operator is never told the tag exists; conversely store.go:3160/version_control.go:465 return `report, err` when only `recomputeBlockedAfterPull` failed — rebase committed, CLI still prints "restored to pre-rebase state". Add `Restored bool` to `RebaseReport`, set only by the defer; gate the message on it; return `report, err` at :141/:145.
- **Deferred reset runs on the caller's context** (rebase.go:125): a canceled API context means the rollback itself can't execute. Use a bounded detached context for cleanup.
- **Merge-error handling diverges from pull-settle** (rebase.go:461-468): bails immediately where `SettleMerge` deliberately carries `mergeErr` through the settle pass because some Dolt versions error on conflicts. On such builds `bd dolt rebase` could never complete (the `child_counters` conflict is always present). Route through the same shape.
- **Temp ID `parent.1000000+i` has no occupancy check** (rebase.go:401-413): a bystander at `parent.1000000.5` gets silently swept into the swapped subtree (probe-confirmed). Assert `temp`/`temp.%` free in issues+wisps, or allocate from the same free-number pool.
- **Counter delete/modify conflict no-ops silently** (rebase.go:531-578): our-side deletion → `UPDATE` affects 0 rows, `--ours` keeps the deletion, counter gone. Upsert like :294-297 + check `RowsAffected`. Also :537's `strings.Contains(err.Error(), ...)` swallows real errors — use `dberrors.IsTableNotExist`.
- **Header comment claims `content_hash` is nulled on renumber** (rebase.go:47-51) — nothing does that (and it's unnecessary: `ComputeContentHash` excludes ID). On a corruption-adjacent path, an asserted-but-absent safety measure is worse than none. Delete the paragraph.
- **Coverage gaps from the previous round remain:** no test exercises `RebaseRemote` on either store; no two-clone convergence test; `--json` prints prose (report has json tags, CLI never checks `jsonOutput`); registration tests not extended; and nothing routes an operator here — the pull-failure path never mentions `bd dolt rebase`. A one-line hint there is the minimum for discoverability.
- Nits: `CountersSet` map iteration makes report output non-deterministic (sort keys); `--dry-run` would be cheap and worth it for an operator recovery command; backup tags accumulate with no documented cleanup.

CI-cost note: the new tests land in `test-embedded-storage` (~4s wall, negligible), not the at-ceiling conformance shards — no concern there.

## Verdict

Not mergeable at this head — blockers 1 and 2 are confirmed corruption on the command's own recovery path. But the deltas are small relative to the value and the invariants that matter (derived-PK dep rekey via `issueops.UpdateIssueIDInTx`, sorted collision processing, backup-tag mechanics) are genuinely satisfied. Want to take these? If you'd rather we absorb them, we're happy to land maintainer-side fixes on top of your branch with your commits intact — say the word.

pr-babysit: delayed-close lane so PR dispositions are offers, not verdicts
---
Measured 2026-07-25: all five sampled 2026 declines closed 0-1s after the disposition comment (gastownhall/beads#4862 1s, #4884 0s, #4286 0s, #4694 1s, #4439 1s), and none of 17 contributors replied to any written decline in the window - even though every one thanked them, named the specific value, preserved attribution and offered a route back. Contrast gastownhall/beads#77 (2025-10-18): steveyegge posted the decline and left it open; maphew replied 8h later and asked for the close himself, then shipped maphew/beads-ui three days later. The open door IS the mechanism.

Proposal: a third patrol lane alongside merge-when-green / merge-blocked, same fail-closed shape as rearm_sweep().

Handoff (agent, in-session): post the disposition comment, then label the bead 'close-when-quiet' with metadata pr_close_after=<RFC3339>, pr_close_head=<sha>, pr_close_reason=<text>, pr_babysit_repo/pr.

Patrol (scripts/pr-babysit, each 12-min pass):
- now < pr_close_after -> skip silently.
- gh unavailable/malformed -> retain (never close on missing data).
- PR already CLOSED or MERGED -> close the bead, log.
- contributor commented, reviewed, or moved the head since the disposition -> remove close-when-quiet, unclaim, so bd ready surfaces it. A contributor who engaged gets a human, not a timer.
- otherwise, window elapsed and silent -> gh pr close with pr_close_reason, close the bead.

Budget/escalation mirrors the existing counters: cap retained passes, escalate to a labelled stop rather than looping.
